sets.set: Git forms of the surface record

examples.input:
$'it\'s' cat <<-EOF
	body
	EOF
 case $x in a) git add . ;; *) ;; esac ${name:-default} && exec -a name git gc
if true; then grep -Fq x <<<"$output" eval "git stash list" x=$(echo "$(git describe)") a\ b )

echo "a $b c" grep -Fq x <<<"$output" cat <<-EOF
	body
	EOF
 echo "a $b c" echo "a $b c" 2>&1

& `git branch --show-current` $'tab\there' cat <<'EOF'
body $x
EOF
 VAR=1 OTHER='two words' env git diff echo "a $b c"

$'tab\there' exec -a name git gc ( cat <<'EOF'
body $x
EOF
 git status $(git rev-parse HEAD)
$'tab\there' for f in *.md; do { grep -Fq x <<<"$output" > out.txt $((1 + 2))

grep -Fq x <<<"$output" cat <<EOF
body $x
EOF
 $'it\'s' bash -c 'git log -1' $((1 + 2)) grep -Fq x <<<"$output"

defects.ansi-quote: the old reader took $'...' as a dollar and a single-quoted text, so an escaped quote inside it ended the quote early and an escape kept its backslash
defects.here-string: the old reader took a here-string (<<<) as a here-document and read the rest of the text as its body, so every command after it was unread
defects.ansi-quote and here-string: both of the defects above in one text
